checkpoint_finding.future_project_fit_rule: A fit on GSE281160 is continual_seen for its retained cells, targets, guides, covariates, and expression outcomes. Only compositions, doses, or contexts whose atomic perturbations were learned in the outer training role may be queried.

preprocessing_and_evaluation_incidents.finding: setup_anndata enumerates perturbation atoms and covariate categories from the entire AnnData before the model's train/validation/OOD split.
A held target included only as an OOD category receives an untrained categorical embedding; this is not a learned unseen-target representation.
The setup path can register differential-expression metadata; benchmark DE features and endpoints must not be derived from outer evaluation outcomes.
The frozen categorical genetic path has no noncoding sequence or guide encoder and therefore cannot represent a wholly unseen target locus.

prediction_first_rule.gse313774: Bulk liver-chip libraries cannot be passed as single cells or matched to the GSE281160 locus vocabulary. No CPA stress score is allowed without a new assay-native and perturbation-matched preregistration before outcome opening.

remaining_blockers: Keep CPA unscheduled for the current held-target task; register a seen-atom held-combination, dose, or context task before fitting.
Build perturbation and covariate vocabularies from outer-training data only and reject unknown atoms.
Resolve biological replicates, matrix layer, likelihood, gene order, control category, dose coding, and covariates.
Freeze architecture, adversarial schedule, optimizer, seeds, predictive sampling rule, output scale, and trained weight hashes.
Resolve the BSD-3-Clause LICENSE versus MIT pyproject metadata conflict before open derivative release.
Pass isolated legacy scvi runtime, save/resume, grouped split, and unknown-target rejection fixtures.

systema_audit.rule: Compute O_pert from training perturbation-specific replicate centroids in the independent evaluator. Predictive samples do not count as biological replicates.
